question: What are the latest developments in AI data center infrastructure?

response.answer:
The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence is transforming data centers into major drivers of electricity demand, prompting the exploration of alternative models such as floating and offshore data centers in marine environments to exploit natural cooling and direct offshore renewable energy integration. [1]

The transition toward geo-distributed AI training across multiple data centers is being driven by model growth and data sovereignty requirements, utilizing EVPN-VXLAN infrastructure foundations alongside scalable emulation frameworks to handle synchronization and wide-area latency challenges. [2]

Researchers are also addressing power constraints and infrastructure planning by linking high-resolution workload power measurements—such as those for NVIDIA H100 GPU-based training, fine-tuning, and inference—to whole-facility energy demand. [3]

question: What is emerging in liquid cooling and power availability?

response.answer: AI workloads are accelerating the data center transition toward high-density racks using direct-to-chip (DTC) liquid cooling for chilled-water and warm-water architectures [S1]. Furthermore, GPU-dense AI data centers are adopting liquid cooling to handle extreme heat loads [S2, S4], while evolving toward gigawatt grid loads characterized by highly fluctuating power swings [S4]. [1] [2] [3]
